# Hardware and porting

Porting the stack to an MCU family, bringing up a board, working with vendor-generated code, and what shipping firmware
must do on the hardware. The MCU port lives in kb-core's interfaces/mcu/&lt;family&gt;/; the board side is in the board
HAL's bind.

## KB-HW-001: Every MCU family implements the foundation interfaces { #kb-hw-001 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The foundation set is new to the Kokeb standard.

**MUST** · library · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Each real MCU family in `interfaces/mcu/<family>/` implements `BaseSpi`, `BaseI2c`, `BaseGpio`, `BaseAdc`, `BaseNvs`,
`BaseLogger`, `BaseTemperature` and `BasePeriodicTimer`. Other `Base*` interfaces are implemented when the MCU has the
hardware and a consumer needs it; there are no stubs, and enabling one the family lacks fails at CMake configure time.

*Why:* Every handler, manager and HAL then compiles on a new family without change. A stub that compiles but does
nothing turns a configuration mistake into a bench fault.

*Verified by:*

- `mcu-foundation-set` (planned): each real family under interfaces/mcu/ implements the eight foundation Base\*
  interfaces, and enabling an optional one the family lacks fails at CMake configure time

*See also:* [ADR-0014](../adr/0014-three-kinds-of-specific.md)

*Explained in:* [standards/library.md](../standards/library.md#interfaces)

## KB-HW-002: A port passes the conformance suite before it is done { #kb-hw-002 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · library, hal · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A new or changed MCU port passes the `Base*` conformance tests: on the host against a mocked vendor SDK where the SDK
allows, and as loopback tests on a board (SPI MOSI to MISO, UART TX to RX, GPIO pairs). After a port, vendor-callback
wiring, MCU-gated drivers and the family's build options are re-tested on the board.

*Verified by:*

- `port-conformance` (planned): the Base\* conformance suite passes for the named MCU family, on the host against a
  mocked SDK and, on a scheduled job with a board, as loopback tests
- review: The pull request links the loopback run on a board, or is marked not verified on hardware.

*Explained in:* [checklists/new-board-hal.md](../checklists/new-board-hal.md)

## KB-HW-003: The port owns vendor-callback bridging, one entry point per interrupt family { #kb-hw-003 }

**MUST** · library, hal · since 1.0

The family's port bridges vendor callbacks (`HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback`, DMA completion) to its objects through a static
dispatch table or a handle lookup, with one documented entry point per interrupt family. The bridge takes no mutex; it
sets an `OsEventFlags` bit or gives a `SignalSemaphore` and returns.

*Verified by:*

- review: Each interrupt family has one entry point documented in the port header, and no code reached from it takes a
  mutex.

*Explained in:* [standards/threading-and-timing.md](../standards/threading-and-timing.md#one-lock)

## KB-HW-004: Configure peripherals the way the vendor SDK expects { #kb-hw-004 }

**GUIDE** · library, hal · since 1.0

Where the vendor's culture is a configuration tool (STM32CubeMX, MCUXpresso), the port wraps the generated handles;
where the SDK has a full run-time API (ESP-IDF), the port configures the peripheral itself from a spec. Either way the
rest of the stack sees only the `Base*` interface.

*Explained in:* [standards/library.md](../standards/library.md#interfaces)

## KB-HW-005: Clock speeds and bus settings come from configuration, not literals { #kb-hw-005 }

**SHOULD** · library, hal · since 1.0

A port object takes clock speed, mode and pins from its constructor spec or the board config; it hard-codes none of
them.

*Verified by:*

- review: Bus clocks, modes and pins in the port come from the spec or the board config.

*Explained in:* [standards/hal.md](../standards/hal.md#the-platform-bind)

## KB-HW-006: A port publishes its measured performance { #kb-hw-006 }

**SHOULD** · library · since 1.0

A port's documentation lists measured timings for the foundation operations (an 8-byte SPI transfer, a GPIO set, an ADC
read, a 2-byte I2C transfer, periodic-timer jitter) with the clock rates used, so HAL authors can tell whether a hot
path needs more.

*Verified by:*

- review: The port's documentation has a measured timing table for the foundation operations.


## KB-HW-007: A board HAL starts from a complete hardware picture { #kb-hw-007 }

**GUIDE** · hal · since 1.0

Before writing a board HAL, have the schematic and pin-out, the full chip list, the chosen MCU variant, and a released
driver and kb-core support for every chip and peripheral on the board. A missing peripheral goes into kb-core first.

*Explained in:* [checklists/new-board-hal.md](../checklists/new-board-hal.md)

## KB-HW-008: STM32 ports use CubeMX, the STM32 HAL, CMake and FreeRTOS by default { #kb-hw-008 }

**GUIDE** · library, hal · since 1.0

Start an STM32 family with STM32CubeMX for clocks and pins, the STM32 HAL (LL where latency needs it), CMake, and
FreeRTOS or ThreadX at a 1 kHz tick.

*See also:* [ADR-0006](../adr/0006-freertos-1khz-tick.md)


## KB-HW-009: Vendor-generated code is regenerable and never hand-edited outside its markers { #kb-hw-009 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · hal, firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A CubeMX project generates peripheral initialisation as `.c`/`.h` pairs, copies only the needed libraries and never uses
the single-`main.c` option. The `.ioc` and the generated tree are committed; hand-written code goes only between `USER
CODE` markers or in separate files (vendor weak callbacks are overridden in the project's own interrupt file), and any
other patch to generated files is listed in `PATCHES.md`.

*Why:* Regenerating from the `.ioc` must not lose work or silently revert a fix.

*Verified by:*

- `cubemx-discipline` (planned): the .ioc sets ProjectManager.CoupleFile=true and the library-copy option, and
  regenerating from the .ioc reproduces the committed tree except for USER CODE blocks and the patches listed in
  PATCHES.md


## KB-HW-010: Heavily used buses use DMA, with a timed-out polled fallback { #kb-hw-010 }

**SHOULD** · library, hal · since 1.0

SPI, I2C and UART ports use DMA when the board wires a DMA channel and fall back to polled transfers otherwise; both
paths have a timeout and both are tested.

*Verified by:*

- review: The DMA and polled paths both have a timeout and a test.


## KB-HW-011: Hardware and protocol changes update the specification in the same pull request { #kb-hw-011 }

**SHOULD** · driver, hal, firmware · since 1.0

A change that follows a hardware or protocol change updates the affected Hardware page, board specification or protocol
description in the same pull request.

*Verified by:*

- review: The Hardware or protocol documentation matches the change.


## KB-HW-012: Shipping firmware enables the watchdog, serviced from a supervisor task { #kb-hw-012 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Release firmware enables the hardware or task watchdog, and one supervisor task services it only while the tasks it
watches report progress.

*Why:* A hung task with a live actuator must end in a reset, not a stuck output.

*Verified by:*

- `sdkconfig-defaults/watchdog` (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz
  is CONFIG\_FREERTOS\_HZ=1000)
- review: The supervisor services the watchdog only when every watched task has reported.


## KB-HW-013: Shipping firmware configures brownout reset { #kb-hw-013 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Release firmware enables brownout detection with reset, at a threshold above the board's minimum supply.

*Verified by:*

- `sdkconfig-defaults/brownout` (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz
  is CONFIG\_FREERTOS\_HZ=1000)


## KB-HW-014: Over-the-air updates verify signatures and can roll back { #kb-hw-014 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · firmware · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Firmware that updates over the air keeps the previous image and rolls back to it when the new one fails to confirm
itself. A product that signs its images verifies the signature before booting an update.

*Verified by:*

- `sdkconfig-defaults/ota` (planned): sdkconfig.defaults of every ESP-IDF project sets the named value (freertos-hz is
  CONFIG\_FREERTOS\_HZ=1000)
- review: The good-update and rollback paths were exercised on a board before release.


## KB-HW-015: Firmware logs why it booted and what it is { #kb-hw-015 }

**SHOULD** · firmware · since 1.0

On every start the firmware logs the reset reason from the bind and its own version, release train and provenance
header.

*Verified by:*

- review: The boot log has the reset reason and the version and provenance.

*Explained in:* [standards/product.md](../standards/product.md#releases)

## KB-HW-016: Firmware reports its health and keeps a crash record { #kb-hw-016 }

**SHOULD** · firmware · since 1.0

Firmware captures free heap, the largest free block and uptime periodically in its diagnostics, and persists a crash
record (reason, task, program counter) to NVS or external storage for the next boot.

*Verified by:*

- review: Health figures are in the diagnostics and a crash record survives a reset.


## KB-HW-017: A factory test mode exists and is documented { #kb-hw-017 }

**SHOULD** · firmware · since 1.0

Production firmware has a factory test mode, entered by a documented method (an NVS flag or a button held at boot), and
the product's documentation describes what it tests.

*Verified by:*

- review: The factory mode, how to enter it and what it tests are documented.
